headline: Day two of the liquidation, and the bid has moved to the front end: 2y +11bp, 2s10s flatter, MOVE through 100 — and the metals dump has spread into the entire hard-asset equity complex.
summary: The composition of the rates shock changed today, and that matters more than the size. Yesterday was a long-end/term-premium story; today the front end led. The 2-year jumped 11bp to 4.92% (+58bp in a month, +145bp YTD, z=1.88), the 5-year +8bp to 5.06%, while 10s and 30s added only 7bp each to 5.24% and 5.56%. 2s10s flattened 4bp to 32bp. A bear flattener with the 3-month bill up 38bp on the month is the market pricing a policy mistake in the other direction — not more supply, but a hike. The rates composite deteriorated to -83 from -76 and risk regime slipped to -15. The 10-year real yield is 2.90%, +48bp on the month (z=1.89, acceleration 1.39), 37% above its 200-day. MOVE broke 100 for the first time in this episode, 101.82, +43.5% on the month with z=2.37 and acceleration 1.69. Equity vol finally stopped ignoring it: VIX +8.1% to 16.07, VIX/VIX3M +6.3% with acceleration 1.46. Vol is now confirming rates on both legs.

Precious metals day two was not a stabilization, it was a broadening. Gold -3.7% to 4,160 (acceleration z=-3.05, -8.2% on the month, 8.8% below its 200-day), silver -5.1% to 60.95 and now 16.3% below its 200-day, platinum -2.9%. GDX -5.4%, GDXJ -5.8%, NEM -4.4% with acceleration -3.24, GDX/gold accelerating at -3.02. The new information is the contagion into industrial hard assets: XME -2.7% (-11.2% on the month, acceleration -2.31), COPX -1.7% (-9.7%, acceleration -2.26), REMX -3.3% (-16.7% on the month, 4th percentile), NLR -12.0% on the month with acceleration -2.36 at the 2nd percentile, URA -11.9%. That is margin and momentum unwind, not a commodity demand signal — copper itself only fell 1.2% and copper/gold rose another 2.6% to the 98.5th percentile. Growth pulse is unchanged at +17, XLI/XLU sits at the 98.6th percentile, oil/gold +5.1% (+22.1% on the month). Still not a growth scare. WTI +1.2% to 93.55 even as Brent printed -4.9% and RBOB -6.7% (-9.3% on the month), and 5-year breakevens ticked down 1bp to 2.33% at the 30th percentile. The real-yield surge is real, not inflationary — which is exactly why it hurts collateral rather than cyclicals.

Inside equities the derate is now concentrated in leverage and in last month's winners, while the index barely moves. SPX -0.8% to 7,683.7 but only -0.4% on the month and still 6.5% above its 200-day at the 92nd percentile. Underneath: META -4.8% after a +23.9% month (z=1.89), AMD -3.6% (still 65% above its 200-day), TSLA -3.9%, ORCL -3.3% and -12.1% on the month, BA -6.9%, ITA -10.0% on the month with z=-2.09, NFLX -2.7%. Financials keep bleeding: XLF -1.2% (-6.4% on the month, z=-1.53), BX -3.3% and -19.5% on the month (z=-2.02), GS -2.0% (-10.9%), JPM -1.9%, IAI -8.3% on the month, KIE -6.8%. Breadth is at the worst of the cycle: RSP/SPY z=-2.06 (-4.4% on the month, 9th percentile), IWM/SPY -4.8%, IYT/SPY z=-2.16 at the 2nd percentile, DJT -8.4% on the month. Credit duration is pinned at the lows — LQD and IEF both at the 0th percentile, TLT 78.62 at the 0th percentile — while HYG/IEF still sits at the 96th percentile. The stress is the discount rate, not defaults.

What survives is narrow and identifiable: AI hardware and healthcare. NVDA +1.7%, ASML +1.6%, TSM +0.5%, SMH +8.5% on the month with SMH/SPY z=1.11, Taiwan's TAIEX at the 99th percentile and EWT +5.8% on the month. XLV +0.3%, IBB +0.4%, XBI +1.0%, UNH and LLY green. Crypto is quietly resilient against a rising dollar — BTC 83,025 (-1.7% today but +6.9% on the month, +41.8% on three), MSTR +23.4% on the month, ETH/BTC +2.9% — though all three still sit in the bottom 37% of their 52-week range. The dollar is the transmission channel: DXY +0.2% to 101.22 with acceleration 1.00, USDCHF at a 52-week high, EURUSD at the 3rd percentile, and USDMXN +1.3% to 17.974, +6.0% on the month with z=2.31 and acceleration 2.15 — a fifth consecutive session of accelerating EM FX pain that took EZA -3.0%, TUR -2.6% and INDA -1.6% with it. Trade the gap between an index 6.5% above its 200-day and a leverage complex derating at z=-2.

good.text: Still not a growth scare: copper/gold +2.6% to the 98.5th percentile (+9.7% on the month), oil/gold +5.1% (+22.1%), XLI/XLU at the 98.6th percentile, growth pulse unchanged at +17. Copper fell only 1.2% while gold fell 3.7% — the metals dump is positioning, not demand.

Credit risk has not joined credit duration. HYG/IEF +1.0% on the month at the 96th percentile, BKLN +0.3% on the month at the 91st percentile despite a -0.3% day. Spreads are behaving; it is the discount rate doing the damage.
AI hardware leadership held through a -0.8% tape: NVDA +1.7%, ASML +1.6%, TSM +0.5%, SMH +8.5% on the month with SMH/SPY z=1.11, Taiwan TAIEX at the 99th percentile and EWT +5.8% on the month.

Healthcare is being bought as the new defensive now that utilities and staples have failed: XLV +0.3% with relative strength turning up, IBB +0.4%, XBI +1.0%, UNH +0.3%, LLY +0.1% — against XLU -7.5% and XLP -3.1% on the month.

Inflation expectations refuse to confirm the yield move: 5-year breakeven -1bp to 2.33% at the 30th percentile, 10-year flat at 2.34%, gasoline -9.3% and wheat -10.2% on the month. The real-yield spike is a term-premium and policy story, not a CPI story.
Crypto is holding against a rising dollar, an unusual tell: BTC +6.9% on the month and +41.8% on three months, ETH +10.0%, MSTR +23.4%, ETH/BTC +2.9% — all with trends still turning up.

bad.text: The curve is bear-flattening: 2-year +11bp to 4.92% (+58bp on the month, z=1.88), 5-year +8bp to 5.06%, 3-month +38bp on the month, 2s10s -4bp to 32bp. Front-end-led selling is hike risk, a strictly worse regime than the long-end supply story of last week. Rates composite -83.

Volatility has confirmed. MOVE broke 100 to 101.82, +43.5% on the month with z=2.37 and acceleration 1.69; VIX +8.1% to 16.07; VIX/VIX3M +6.3% with acceleration 1.46. Accelerating bond vol with equity vol finally following is the definition of an unhedged tape.

The hard-asset liquidation broadened from metals into miners and the whole power/materials theme: gold acceleration -3.05, silver -5.1%, GDX -5.4%, GDXJ -5.8%, NEM acceleration -3.24, XME acceleration -2.31, COPX -2.26, REMX -16.7% on the month, NLR -12.0% at the 2nd percentile, URA -11.9%.

Duration and IG credit are pinned at 52-week lows with no bounce: LQD -0.7% at the 0th percentile (-3.2% on the month), IEF at the 0th percentile (z=-1.53), TLT -0.9% to 78.62 at the 0th percentile, HYG rolling over at z=-1.44.

Breadth is the worst of the cycle and got no repair: RSP/SPY z=-2.06 at the 9th percentile, IWM/SPY -4.8% on the month, IYT/SPY z=-2.16 at the 2nd percentile, DJT -8.4%, equal-weight S&P -4.6%. The index is 6.5% above its 200-day on a shrinking base.

The EM FX squeeze is accelerating for a fifth session: USDMXN +1.3% to 17.974 (+6.0% on the month, z=2.31, acceleration 2.15), USDBRL +0.7%, CEW -0.5%, USDCHF at a 52-week high, EURUSD at the 3rd percentile — and the equity follow-through is showing up in EZA -3.0%, TUR -2.6%, INDA -1.6%.

trades.name: Short the front end (2-year)
trades.line: Short ZT / 2y notes: bear flattener says hike, not supply
trades.expr: Short Dec 2-year note futures (ZT), or buy Dec/Mar SOFR put spreads; cash proxy is short SHY against a flat 10y position (short ZT vs long TY at 2:1 duration to isolate the flattener).
trades.thesis: The marginal seller has moved from the 30-year to the 2-year. With the 3-month bill up 38bp on the month and the 2-year up 58bp to 4.92%, the market is repricing the policy path, not just term premium. That has further to run than the long end, which is already 100th percentile and crowded short.
trades.trigger: 2y +11bp today (z=1.88, acceleration 1.25) while 30y added only 7bp; 2s10s flattened 4bp to 32bp; MOVE through 100 at z=2.37; breakevens flat at 2.33%, so this is real-rate/policy repricing.
trades.stop: 2-year back below 4.70% or 2s10s steepening through 45bp with MOVE back under 90 — that would mean the front end is done and the story reverts to supply.

trades.name: Own convexity while vol confirms
trades.line: Buy Nov VIX 20/28 call spread; equity vol is cheap vs MOVE
trades.expr: Buy November VIX 20/28 call spreads (or Nov SPY 3% OTM put spreads funded by selling 8% OTM puts). Size 30-50bp premium. Avoid outright VIXY carry.
trades.thesis: MOVE at 101.82 (+43.5% on the month) versus VIX at 16.07 in the 15th percentile of its year is the widest cross-asset vol dislocation of this episode. Historically the bond-vol impulse drags equity vol; today was the first day the term structure accelerated (VIX/VIX3M +6.3%, acceleration 1.46) alongside it.
trades.trigger: VIX +8.1% and VIX3M +1.7% — the curve steepening at the front means hedges are being bought; SPX still only -0.4% on the month, so premium hasn't repriced.
trades.stop: VIX/VIX3M back below 0.83 with MOVE under 90 and SPX making a new high — kill the structure for half premium.
trades.target: VIX 22-25 on a 3-4% index drawdown; 2-3x on the spread.

trades.name: Long loans / short high yield & IG
trades.line: Long BKLN, short HYG+LQD: own spread, not duration
trades.expr: Long BKLN, short a duration-matched basket of HYG and LQD (roughly 60/40 by notional, ~1.2x BKLN notional to equalize vol).
trades.thesis: Every dollar of pain in credit this month is discount rate, not default risk. Floating-rate loans capture the front-end repricing that is killing the fixed-rate index; HYG/IEF at the 96th percentile tells you spreads are fine, so short the duration and own the coupon reset.
trades.trigger: LQD -0.7% and at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range (-3.2% on the month, z=-1.31), IEF also 0th percentile, while BKLN is +0.3% on the month at the 91st percentile; 2y +58bp on the month resets loan coupons higher.
trades.stop: HYG/IEF breaking below its 200-day (-3.2% from here) or BKLN losing 20.20 — that signals genuine credit stress and the pair inverts.
trades.target: 300-400bp of relative return; add if HY OAS widens without loans following.

trades.name: Long gold vs short silver
trades.line: Long GLD / short SLV: ratio 68 heading to 74 in a liquidation
trades.expr: Long GLD, short silver futures or SLV at 1:1 dollar notional; scale to 1.3x short silver if using vol-weighting.
trades.thesis: When the precious complex is being liquidated for margin rather than sold on fundamentals, the high-beta leg loses twice. Silver is already 16.3% below its 200-day versus gold's 8.8%, and the ratio has turned up. This monetizes day three of the unwind without betting on a bottom in bullion.
trades.trigger: Silver -5.1% versus gold -3.7% today; gold/silver +1.5% to 68.26 and turning up (acceleration 0.44); silver acceleration z=-1.91, platinum -2.9%; GDX/gold acceleration -3.02 shows equity holders still forced sellers.
trades.stop: Gold/silver back under 65, or real yields (DFII10) falling 20bp from 2.90% — a real-yield reversal lifts silver hardest.

trades.name: Short housing at a 7% mortgage
trades.line: Short ITB, long puts on HD: 7.03% mortgage, 2.90% real yield
trades.expr: Short ITB (or XHB), plus January HD 270 puts for the retail-remodel leg. Pair against long SPY if you want the sector isolated.
trades.thesis: Housing is the cleanest cash-flow victim of a 2.90% real 10-year. The 30-year mortgage is back to 7.03%, up 38bp in a month, and builders are already breaking trend rather than merely underperforming — there's no valuation support and no rate relief priced.
trades.trigger: ITB -0.8% and -7.2% on the month at the 13th percentile, XHB/SPY at the 3rd percentile (-6.2% on the month), DHI -1.5%, HD -1.1% and -11.6% on the month sitting at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range; mortgage rate at the 100th percentile.
trades.stop: 10-year real yield below 2.65% or XHB reclaiming its 200-day (+7.8% from here).

trades.name: Long energy majors vs short transports
trades.line: Long XOM+CVX / short IYT: $93 crude, freight rolling over
trades.expr: Long an equal-weight XOM/CVX basket (or XLE), short IYT at equal dollar notional.
trades.thesis: Crude at 93.55 is a cost for the freight complex and a cash flow for the majors. Energy relative strength is +12.6% over three months and turning up; transports are the single weakest relative line in the entire digest. This pays whether the tape is risk-on or risk-off, because it is an input-cost spread, not a beta bet.
trades.trigger: XOM +1.2% and CVX +0.9% on a -0.8% SPX day, XLE relative strength turning up; against IYT -8.3% on the month (z=-1.59), IYT/SPY z=-2.16 at the 2nd percentile, DJT -8.4%, FDX -12.1% on the month, UPS -10.5%, XTN -7.2%.
trades.stop: WTI below 84 (breaking its 200-day extension) or IYT/SPY reclaiming its 200-day — a genuine freight demand upturn would flip both legs.

trades.name: Short the leverage complex vs healthcare
trades.line: Short XLF & BX / long XLV: leverage derates, care re-rates
trades.expr: Short XLF plus a satellite short in BX, long XLV at equal notional (2/3 XLF, 1/3 BX versus 1x XLV).
trades.thesis: Rising front-end rates with flattening curve and 100+ MOVE compress exactly the businesses that live on leverage, deal flow and mark-to-market carry. Healthcare is the only defensive whose relative strength is turning up now that utilities and staples have broken. This is the cleanest way to short the derate without shorting the index at the 92nd percentile.
trades.trigger: XLF -1.2% today and -6.4% on the month (z=-1.53, relative strength rolling over), BX -3.3% and -19.5% on the month (z=-2.02), GS -10.9%, IAI -8.3%, KIE -6.8%, KRE/SPY at the 32nd percentile — against XLV +0.3% with relative strength turning up and +3.3% over three months.
trades.stop: 2s10s steepening past 50bp with KRE/SPY back above its 200-day, or XLV breaking below its 200-day.
